prompt: We're Aster Cycles, a 14-person e-bike maker in Rotterdam. In March we launch the Aster C1, a €6,200 carbon commuter e-bike (10.9 kg, belt drive, integrated lights). Audience: design-minded city commuters 30-50 who'd never buy "sporty" gear — they read Monocle, they care about craft and calm. I want the launch page to feel engineered and quiet, like a precision instrument, not an extreme-sports ad. We have no fonts budget, so everything has to be free for commercial use. Before anyone codes anything, give me the creative direction and the typography + spacing system for a single launch page, as files in a studio/ folder. Don't build the site yet.
assertions: A creative direction file exists in studio/ containing a one-sentence concept specific to Aster (engineered, quiet / precision instrument), not a generic tagline
The palette lists hex values with roles AND contrast ratios that were actually computed (a script or calculation is shown or run), with body text pairs at least 4.5:1

Every chosen font has its licence stated AND checked against a source during the run (npm/Fontsource licence field, Google Fonts/OFL, Fontshare API or licence page), and all are free for commercial use
The typography system defines a fluid type scale using clamp() values with explicit min/max viewport assumptions, plus line-height and letter-spacing per step
A spacing/grid system defines a base unit or scale, grid columns per breakpoint, container width(s) and section spacing
Motion guidance includes durations/easing and an explicit prefers-reduced-motion behaviour
The direction includes an explicit list of things deliberately not done (e.g. avoiding sporty/extreme-sports clichés)
No website implementation code (components, pages, CSS for sections) was created — only direction/system documents (and optionally a token CSS file)
